title: Streaming and the Binge
objective: After this level you can explain how streaming changed when, where and how people watch, and how series were written for binge viewing.
summary: Netflix went from DVDs by mail (1997) to streaming (2007) to whole seasons at once (2013). Autoplay made binge-watching easy, and writers began shaping seasons like one long film.

cards.headline: In 2013, a whole season arrived on the same day.
cards.body: In February 2013 Netflix made all 13 first-season episodes of House of Cards available at once, instead of one a week. You no longer waited for the network's schedule. How did watching get here, and what did it do to the shows themselves?

cards.headline: From the mailbox to the stream
cards.body: Netflix was founded in 1997 by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph as a DVD-rental service: subscribers ordered online and received discs by mail. In 2007 it introduced streaming, letting subscribers watch directly over the Internet. Viewers quickly embraced having all of a new season to watch at their own pace, on whatever screen they wished. The schedule moved from the network to you.

cards.headline: Bingeing is older than streaming
cards.body: To binge-watch is to watch many or all episodes of a series in rapid succession. It predates Netflix: cable networks aired marathons of classic shows in the late 1990s, and binging became routine with TV on DVD a decade later. Streaming made it effortless: on Netflix, the next episode queues up as soon as the last one ends.

cards.headline: Writing a 10-hour movie
cards.body: Broadcast writers build peril at the end of each act to keep you watching through the commercial break. Binge viewers don't need that pull, and they skip the 'previously on' recap. Writer Marc Bernardin notes that writers now describe planning a streaming season as 'breaking a 10-hour movie'. How you watch changed what gets written.

cards.headline: Streaming: binged
learned: House of Cards released a whole season at once in 2013
Bingeing began with cable marathons and DVDs
Streaming seasons are written like one long movie

questions.prompt: Put these steps in Netflix's story in order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Netflix began in 1997 as a DVD-rental service, introduced streaming in 2007, and released all of House of Cards' first season at once in 2013.

questions.prompt: How did binge viewing change the way series are written?

options.label: Writers added more recaps at the start of each episode
Writers began planning a season like one long movie
Every episode had to end at a commercial break
options.rationale: Act-break peril is the broadcast habit binge shows need less.

options.label: Episodes were cut to 10 minutes each
options.rationale: The '10-hour movie' is the whole season, not one episode.

questions.explanation: Binge viewers don't need act-break hooks or recaps; writers speak of 'breaking a 10-hour movie'.

questions.prompt: Around 1903, film exchanges leased prints to theaters instead of selling them. How did Netflix first rent films and shows to its customers?

options.label: It leased film prints to movie theaters
It sold monthly subscriptions to its own cable channel
options.rationale: Netflix began as a DVD-by-mail service, not a cable channel.

options.label: It sent DVDs by mail to subscribers who ordered online
It rented tapes from shops on every corner

questions.explanation: Both were middlemen that rented rather than sold: exchanges leased prints to theaters, and Netflix mailed DVDs to subscribers.
